title: Wordfence report, via Cyber Security News: fake WordPress plugin hides itself, bypasses login checks and relays attacker JavaScript to visitors
date_note: Cyber Security News (25 November) says the underlying Wordfence report is dated 24 November; the Wordfence page itself could not be read.
geo_basis: The article gives no location for the researchers.
summary: Cyber Security News, relaying a Wordfence report, says a fake WordPress plugin creates a login session for an existing account without password or 2FA checks and hides from the dashboard's plugin list. For logged-out visitors it relays JavaScript from an attacker-controlled server. Wordfence found it in two incident response investigations, in January and September 2026; the article says phishing or redirects are possible uses, not confirmed outcomes.
plain: Wordfence reports a fake WordPress plugin that hides itself, lets an attacker log in without a password or 2FA, and serves attacker JavaScript to visitors. Harm beyond that is only a possible use.
exec: A hidden plugin backdoor on WordPress sites can survive an administrator password change, according to the Wordfence report as relayed.
action: Cyber Security News lists these cleanup steps: compare the dashboard plugin list with wp-content/plugins/, keep logs, remove the plugin, review administrator accounts, then rotate credentials and revoke existing sessions after cleanup.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News read; the Wordfence original (named in the article) returned no content to this run.

review.note: action advice: steps were attributed to Wordfence but article attributes them to no one; now attributed to Cyber Security News. Rest matches
